text_blocks.snippet: Invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC) is the most common type of breast cancer, accounting for about 80% of cases. It originates in the milk ducts of the breast and can spread to surrounding tissues or lymph nodes.

list.snippet: Symptoms: Lump in the breast, thickening or redness of the breast skin, nipple discharge
Treatment: Surgery, radiation therapy, chemotherapy, hormone therapy, targeted therapy
Prognosis: Early detection and treatment significantly improve the chances of survival
Location: IDC is most commonly found in the upper outer quadrant of the breast
Risk factors: Age, family history, hormonal factors, lifestyle factors

text_blocks.snippet: It's important to note that other less common types of breast cancer exist, such as invasive lobular carcinoma, ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS), and triple-negative breast cancer.
